name: Take and manage insurance medical evidence orders
sector: medical laboratory and health services (insurance medical evidence)
function: insurance solutions order desk and case management
summary: When a life insurer needs medical evidence before it can underwrite an application, the advisor or the insurer orders a paramedical exam, a tele-interview, an attending physician statement (APS) or an inspection report from the company. Case coordinators at the order desk check each order, key the ones that arrive by email, fax or phone, look for duplicates, assign a nearby health professional, phone applicants to book tele-interviews and set up APS and inspection requests, while keeping the advisor's status screen current. The work is fast per order but high volume, and most delay comes from incomplete orders, examiners who decline assignments in thin areas and applicants who do not answer scheduling calls.

baseline.org_archetype: The insurance medical evidence business line of a large Canadian laboratory company, serving every Canadian life insurer through an order management system, a national network of employed and contracted examiners and a tele-interview centre.
baseline.notes: One order is one service order (paramedical, tele-interview, APS or inspection), as the company's web ordering takes each service separately. The process ends when the order is dispatched to the fulfilment team or closed; booking the exam appointment, chasing APS clinics and releasing results belong to the linked processes.

trigger: An advisor or insurer submits a medical evidence order online, by insurer feed, email, fax or phone.
end_state: The order is assigned to an examiner who accepted it, booked as a tele-interview, released to the APS or inspection team, or closed as cancelled, duplicate, incomplete or unable to contact, with the status visible in iCARE.

volume.seasonality: Busier in January to March and in the autumn as advisors close sales before year end and RRSP season; quieter in July and August and over the December holidays.

evidence.note: Taken from the organisation file's insurance orders driver (28,000 to 48,000 a month), itself an estimate; seasonality is the author's estimate.

roles.title: Case coordinator (insurance orders and examiner assignment)
roles.department: Insurance order desk and case management

evidence.note: Customer care representatives assign health professionals and contact applicants (dyn_adv, dyn_car). FTE: about 58 of the 70 coordinators, sized so stated FTE is close to hands-on time times 38,000 orders; the rest work on examiner follow-up and case release. Wage near the Job Bank 13112 Ontario median; Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

roles.title: Team lead, insurance customer care
roles.department: Insurance order desk and case management

evidence.note: Team leads handle coverage gaps and aged orders for roughly 14 percent of paramedical orders plus queue supervision; share of the 12 team leads is an estimate. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

roles.title: Manager, insurance case management
roles.department: Insurance solutions (The model laboratory's insurance testing service)

evidence.note: Managers approve travel surcharges and out-of-network arrangements for a few percent of paramedical orders; estimate. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

roles.title: Account manager, insurance carriers and advisors
roles.department: Insurance solutions (The model laboratory's insurance testing service)

evidence.note: Account managers answer carrier-specific requirement questions on about 3 percent of orders; estimate. Loaded cost is the organisation file's hourly wage times 1.35 (benefits, payroll taxes and overhead).

systems.name: Insurance Order Management System with Paraweb ordering and iCARE status hub
Tele-interview scheduler and interview questionnaire software
Contact centre telephony with IVR, queues and call recording
Health professional portal and examiner availability calendar (part of OMS)

steps.name: Receive order in the order management system
steps.description: An advisor or insurer submits a paramedical, tele-interview, APS or inspection order through the web ordering screens or an insurer's electronic feed, which creates an order record in the OMS with an order number and posts a 'received' status to iCARE. Email, fax and phone orders arrive in a shared intake queue instead and are not yet in the OMS.
inputs: web order form or insurer electronic order
outputs: order record or intake queue item

error.defect_description: None at this step; data quality depends on the orderer.

next.condition: placed online or by insurer feed
received by email, fax or phone

evidence.note: Channels and 24/7 web ordering stated by the company; the 75/25 split between web and manual channels is the author's estimate for 2019-2022.

steps.name: Key email, fax or phone order into OMS
steps.description: A case coordinator opens the faxed requisition, email or phone notes, creates the order in the OMS and types the applicant's name, date of birth, address, phone numbers, language, insurer, policy or application number, advisor code and the requirement codes. Handwritten faxes are often hard to read, so the coordinator compares the fields with the insurer's requirement form.

error.defect_description: Mistyped phone number, date of birth or requirement code.

evidence.note: Email and phone ordering stated (dyn_adv); fax remained a common channel for applications in SOA 2011. Times are the author's estimate for keying about 15 fields.

steps.name: Check order completeness and requirement codes
steps.description: The coordinator opens the order, confirms that the applicant can be reached (at least one valid phone number and an address), that the insurer and policy number are present and that each requirement code matches a product the insurer has set up (for example its blood profile code, urine only, resting ECG, or the insurer's tele-interview script). Special instructions such as fasting, French-language service or a workplace visit are noted on the order.

error.defect_description: A wrong or missing requirement is not noticed and the examiner collects the wrong items.

control.basis: Carrier service agreements and the order desk procedure: an order is assigned only when applicant identity, contact details, insurer, policy number and valid requirement codes are present

next.condition: contact details, policy number or requirement missing or unclear
requirement code not set up for this insurer or conflicts with its grid
advisor or insurer cancels before dispatch

evidence.note: Order contents listed by the company (dyn_car); rush orders need phone, location, availability and language (dyn_tips). The 11 percent pending share is an estimate below the 37 percent average not-in-good-order rate for paper applications in SOA 2011, because web ordering forces required fields; cancellations before dispatch are an estimate.

steps.name: Ask the advisor or insurer for missing details
steps.description: The coordinator sets the order to 'pending information' in the OMS, which shows on iCARE, and phones or emails the advisor's office or the insurer's new business area naming exactly what is missing, such as a working phone number, the policy number or which blood profile is wanted.

error.defect_description: The request does not name everything that is missing, so a second query is needed.

evidence.note: Incomplete applications go to a pending queue while the advisor tracks down the client (wp2015); iCARE status visible to advisors (dyn_faq). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the advisor or insurer to reply
steps.description: The order waits in the pending queue until the advisor's assistant or the insurer's new business clerk replies by email, phone or by editing the order on the web, often after reaching the applicant first. The coordinator does nothing until a reply arrives or the follow-up date on the aging report comes up.

error.defect_description: The reply supplies another wrong phone number or partial details.

next.condition: no reply by the follow-up date

evidence.note: Missing application data took an average 10.3 days to collect across 62 carriers (ipipeline); order details are usually simpler, so a one-day mode is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Follow up an aged pending order
steps.description: From the daily aging report of pending orders, the coordinator calls or emails the advisor again, records the attempt and, after the carrier's limit (often 30 days or three follow-ups), closes the order as incomplete and notifies the advisor and insurer through iCARE.

error.defect_description: An order is closed although the advisor had replied by another channel.

evidence.note: Common order desk practice of aged-order follow-up and closure; closure share and timing are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Confirm a carrier-specific requirement with the insurer
steps.description: When the requirement code or combination is not set up for that insurer, or looks inconsistent with the insurer's age and amount grid, the account manager emails or calls the carrier's underwriting or new business contact to confirm what to collect and updates the carrier's requirement table if it changed.

error.defect_description: Carrier table updated incompletely, affecting later orders.

evidence.note: Insurers publish their own age and amount grids and change them often (75 percent changed requirements within two years in SOA 2011). Share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Search for duplicate or recent orders on the applicant
steps.description: The coordinator searches the OMS by applicant name and date of birth for open orders or requirements completed in the last 12 months, for the same or another insurer. A duplicate order is linked and cancelled, and when two insurers order at once the coordinator flags the orders so one visit covers both, with the applicant's consent for each insurer.

error.defect_description: Duplicate not found, so the applicant is visited twice and the insurer billed twice.

control.basis: Carrier billing terms: one charge per requirement; recent evidence (within 12 months) reused only when the insurer asks

next.condition: advisor calls or emails for status or a change while the order is open
duplicate of an open order; linked and closed

evidence.note: Evidence completed in the past 12 months may be reused and is shared only when asked (equitable1343, empire_fug). Duplicate and status-call shares are estimates.

steps.name: Answer an advisor status call or change request
steps.description: The coordinator takes an advisor's call or email asking whether the order was received, who the examiner is or when the interview is, or asking to change the applicant's phone number, address or appointment preference, updates the OMS and confirms by email. Many of these questions could be answered in iCARE.

error.defect_description: Change typed on the wrong order or not passed to the examiner.

evidence.note: The company asks advisors to use the order tracker instead of calling, since care staff see the same information (dyn_faq). Elapsed time overlaps the order's other waits, so the wait is set near zero; share is an estimate.

steps.name: Route the order to the service queue
steps.description: The OMS places the order in the work queue for its service type: paramedical and lab collection orders go to the examiner assignment queue, tele-interviews to scheduling, APS orders to APS set-up and inspection or records orders to the inspection team's set-up queue.

error.defect_description: None.

next.condition: inspection, MVR or credit report order

evidence.note: Services are ordered separately (PARA, APS, TI). The shares follow the organisation file's monthly volumes for paramedical (16,000), tele-interview (13,000), APS (8,000) and inspection (1,500) orders.

steps.name: Select and assign a health professional
steps.description: The coordinator looks up the applicant's postal code on the territory map, opens the availability calendar of nearby employed and contracted health professionals, checks language and skills (phlebotomy, ECG equipment) and current load, and assigns the order. Rush and large-amount orders go to examiners with the shortest booking times.

error.defect_description: Assigned to an examiner without ECG equipment or the right language, or outside their area.

control.basis: Examiner credentialing: only health professionals whose licence, phlebotomy and ECG training are on file may receive the requirement

evidence.note: A Customer Care Representative identifies an available Health Professional (dyn_adv, dyn_car). Queue time keeps within the 24 to 48 hour applicant contact standard (dyn_para); times are estimates.

steps.name: Health professional accepts the assignment
steps.description: The assigned examiner sees the order on the health professional portal or phone app and accepts it, or declines because of distance, workload or holidays. Contracted examiners are paid per visit and may leave an assignment unanswered for several hours.

error.defect_description: None.

next.condition: declined, not answered or examiner unavailable

evidence.note: Most of the 1,200+ health professionals are contractors per the organisation file; decline share and response time are the author's estimates.

steps.name: Find a replacement examiner or escalate a coverage gap
steps.description: The team lead reviews unaccepted assignments, calls other examiners in the region, widens the search radius or offers an appointment at a collection centre or partner clinic. For remote addresses the team lead may propose an examiner who charges travel time, which needs manager approval.

error.defect_description: Reassigned to an examiner who also cannot meet the booking standard.

next.condition: rural or remote address needs a travel surcharge or alternate site

evidence.note: Coverage gaps in rural areas are named in the organisation file's network management process; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Approve a travel surcharge or alternate arrangement
steps.description: The case management manager reviews the proposed travel charge or out-of-network examiner against the carrier's fee schedule, approves it or asks the account manager to get the insurer's agreement, and records the approval on the order.

error.defect_description: Surcharge approved that the carrier later refuses to pay.

control.basis: Carrier fee schedules pay only the reasonable cost of required evidence at standard area rates (for example Equitable form 1343 note 6); extra charges need approval

evidence.note: Insurers pay only the reasonable cost of required evidence at standard area rates (equitable1343). Approval step and times are estimates.

steps.name: Release the exam assignment and notify the applicant
steps.description: The OMS marks the order 'assigned', sends the examiner the applicant's contact details and requirements, sends the applicant a text or email that an examiner will call, and updates iCARE for the advisor and insurer.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Text and email confirmations and iCARE status tracking are OMS features stated by the company.

steps.name: Check whether the tele-interview is already booked
steps.description: The tele-interview scheduler checks whether the order already carries an agreed appointment time, which advisors sometimes arrange with the client and type into the order comments. In 2019-2022 there was no self-service booking portal, so all other orders wait for a coordinator to call the applicant.

error.defect_description: None.

next.condition: agreed time already on the order

evidence.note: The self-service scheduler launched in January 2023 to remove callouts and telephone tag (dyn_sched), so in 2019-2022 nearly every interview needed a call; advisors could give the applicant's availability on rush orders (dyn_tips). The 8 percent share is an estimate.

steps.name: Call the applicant to book the tele-interview
steps.description: The coordinator phones the applicant, confirms identity with date of birth and address before mentioning the insurance application, explains the interview, asks for a 30 to 45 minute window and the preferred language, and books the slot in the tele-interview scheduler. Many applicants do not answer calls from unknown numbers during the working day.

error.defect_description: Slot booked in the wrong time zone or language.

control.basis: Privacy procedure: confirm the applicant's identity before discussing the application, consistent with PIPEDA safeguards and consent principles

next.condition: no answer, voicemail or bad time

evidence.note: Callouts and telephone tag were the booking method until the 2023 scheduler (dyn_sched); portal booking saves 2 business days on average (dyn_ti), which implies the calling path takes days. Reach rate and times are estimates.

steps.name: Log the attempt and set the next call
steps.description: The coordinator records the attempt in the OMS, leaves a voicemail with the call-back number and booking link, sends a text or email if the order has one, and sets the next call for a different time of day. After three to five failed attempts the order goes to the advisor.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Vendors send texts with booking links and advise a reminder from the agent after several failed contact attempts (examone2021); call-backs are a common delay (wp2015). Attempt limit and shares are estimates.

steps.name: Tell the advisor the applicant cannot be reached
steps.description: The coordinator sets the iCARE status to 'unable to contact', emails or phones the advisor with the numbers tried and the dates of each attempt, and asks for a better number or a time when the applicant can take a call.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Agents are asked to remind clients when contact attempts fail (examone2021). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the advisor to supply a new contact or time
steps.description: The advisor calls the client and replies with a new number or a time when the applicant can take a call, or tells the order desk to cancel because the client withdrew. Orders with no reply are closed after the carrier's limit.

error.defect_description: New number is also wrong.

next.condition: new contact details or time supplied

evidence.note: Author's estimate of advisor response and withdrawal; applicants who are unreachable often have changed their mind about the policy.

steps.name: Confirm the tele-interview booking
steps.description: The scheduler confirms the slot, sends the applicant a confirmation and reminder by text or email with a list of what to have ready (doctor's name, medications), places the booking in the tele-interviewer's schedule and updates iCARE.

error.defect_description: None.

evidence.note: Portal notifications and the preparation list are described on the company's tele-interview page.

steps.name: Verify the APS authorization and physician details
steps.description: The coordinator checks that the order carries the applicant's signed authorization to release medical information, that the signature date is within the insurer's validity period, and that the physician's name, clinic address and fax number are complete; missing items are requested from the insurer.
outputs: verified APS order or pending order

error.defect_description: Expired or unsigned authorization passes and the clinic rejects the request.

control.basis: PIPEDA consent principle and provincial health information acts (for example Ontario PHIPA): a physician discloses a patient's records to an insurer only with the patient's express consent

evidence.note: The company requires a current and valid authorization and the physician's name and address (dyn_aps); insurers usually order the APS themselves (88 percent in soa2011; equitable1343); express consent for sensitive information (opc_consent). The missing-item share is an estimate.

steps.name: Create the APS request for the APS team
steps.description: The coordinator enters the physician and clinic in the OMS, picks the request type the insurer wants (full chart copy, specific questionnaire or limited period), records whether the insurer pre-approved the physician's fee, attaches the authorization image and releases the request to the APS team's queue, which updates iCARE.

error.defect_description: Wrong clinic or request type selected.

evidence.note: Prior fee approval and request content (dyn_aps); the underwriting service sends the request to the physician and follows up (bcmj2023); APS is a separate order type (dyn_paraweb). Times are estimates.

steps.name: Create the inspection or records request
steps.description: The coordinator checks which report the insurer wants (personal history or financial inspection interview, motor vehicle record or credit report), confirms the applicant's licence number or consent where needed and releases the request to the inspection team.

error.defect_description: Wrong report type or missing licence number.

evidence.note: Inspection reports, motor vehicle records and credit reports are listed services (dyn_car); times are estimates.

steps.name: Process a cancellation
steps.description: When the advisor or insurer cancels the order (application withdrawn, declined on other evidence or moved to accelerated underwriting), the coordinator cancels it in the OMS, recalls any assignment, records the reason so no charge is billed and confirms the cancellation through iCARE.

error.defect_description: Assignment not recalled and the examiner still calls the applicant.

evidence.note: Common practice; cancellation share is an estimate. Applications moved to accelerated paths no longer need fluids (genre2021 describes the shift).

exceptions.name: Incomplete order
exceptions.description: A phone number, policy number, requirement code or APS authorization is missing; the order waits on the advisor or insurer and about 1 in 10 of these is closed incomplete.

exceptions.name: Examiner declines or coverage gap
exceptions.description: The assigned examiner declines or does not answer; the team lead finds another examiner and remote addresses need a manager-approved travel surcharge.

exceptions.name: Applicant cannot be reached for tele-interview booking
exceptions.description: Several calls go unanswered, the advisor is asked for a better number and some orders close as unable to contact.

exceptions.name: Cancellation before dispatch
exceptions.description: The application is withdrawn, declined on other evidence or moved to an accelerated path.

exceptions.name: Requirement not set up for the insurer
exceptions.description: The account manager confirms the requirement with the carrier before the order can proceed.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from order received to dispatch (examiner accepted, interview booked or request released) or closure

evidence.note: Synthesis: the company commits to contacting the applicant within 24 to 48 hours of the order, which leaves the order desk about one business day; self-serve tele-interview booking saves 2 business days on average, so phone-booked interviews take several days. No published distribution was found.

benchmarks.unit: hours from order receipt to first applicant contact (paramedical)
business days saved on average when booked in the self-serve portal
benchmarks.population: Company tele-interview orders after the portal launched in January 2023

benchmarks.unit: average days to collect an outstanding requirement

evidence.note: Shows that order desk handling is a small part of the evidence cycle.

benchmarks.unit: average days from application to decision, full underwriting

pain_points.description: Orders arrive without a working phone number, policy number or the right requirement code, so they sit pending while the advisor tracks down the client.

evidence.note: Pending queues for incomplete applications (wp2015); high not-in-good-order rates on paper applications (soa2011).

pain_points.description: Phone booking of tele-interviews takes several call attempts over days; the self-service scheduler that removed most callouts only arrived in January 2023.

evidence.note: Self-serve booking cuts turnaround by 2 business days on average (dyn_ti); it launched on 9 January 2023 (dyn_sched).

pain_points.description: Advisors phone the desk for status that is already on iCARE, taking coordinator time.

evidence.note: The company asks advisors to use the order tracker instead of calling.

pain_points.description: Contracted examiners decline or ignore assignments in rural areas, so team leads hunt for coverage and approve travel charges.

evidence.note: Author's estimate based on the organisation file's description of rural coverage gaps.

pain_points.description: Manual keying of faxed and emailed orders introduces typos in phone numbers and dates of birth that surface only when the examiner cannot reach the applicant.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; common in re-keyed order entry.

sources.title: Insurance advisors
sources.supports: Advisors order paramedicals, APS and tele-interviews online through the Order Management System, by email or by phone; the OMS offers applicant appointment availability, text and email confirmations and reminders and copying order details; a Customer Care Representative assigns an available Health Professional and contacts the applicant; iCARE order tracking; results to carriers within 48 hours or less.

sources.title: Insurance carriers
sources.supports: Carriers order online, by email or by phone; orders carry applicant, insurance type and company, advisor and agency; a Customer Care Representative identifies an available Health Professional and contacts the applicant; ePara; ACORD and custom result downloads; inspection reports, MVR and credit reports offered.

sources.title: Paramedical services
sources.supports: Client contacted within 24 to 48 hours of receiving the order and appointment booked within 72 hours subject to client availability; carrier notified when the order is completed; paramedical 25 to 35 minutes.

sources.title: Tele-interviews
sources.supports: Advisors and applicants can self-serve tele-interview scheduling through a secure portal after registering on iCARE; booking through the portal reduces turnaround by 2 business days on average compared with the traditional contact method; interview about 25 minutes.

sources.title: Paraweb: place your order and review status
sources.supports: Orders are placed separately for Paramedical Services (PARA), Attending Physician Statements (APS) and Telephone Interviews (TI); real-time web order placement and tracking are available 24/7; order tracking by order or policy number.

sources.title: Frequently asked questions: The model laboratory's insurance testing service order tracker
sources.supports: Advisors can see order status in the order tracker and are asked not to call the customer care line for updates because care staff see the same information; specimens average three business days from collection to results delivered to the carrier.

sources.title: Report of the Society of Actuaries Improving the New Business Process Survey Subcommittee
sources.supports: Survey of 43 US and Canadian direct writers (2010): 80 percent say the producer or their staff orders age and amount requirements, 63 percent the company, 27 percent a tele-interview vendor; 88 percent say the company orders the APS; average 37 percent of paper applications received not in good order; fax still the most common way to send paper applications.

sources.title: Evidence of insurability schedule (form 1343)
sources.publisher: The Equitable Life Insurance Company of Canada
sources.supports: Age and amount grid of paramedical, labs, APS, MVR and financial requirements; requirements based on total coverage applied for plus coverage issued in the past 12 months; evidence completed in the past 12 months may be used; the insurer orders the APS and the advisor is responsible for ordering any other required evidence; only the reasonable cost of required evidence at standard area rates is paid.

sources.title: Field underwriting guide for life and critical illness insurance
sources.supports: Medical requirements completed in the past 12 months can usually be accepted subject to a current non-medical; requirements are shared with other companies only when specifically asked; age and amount requirements are not arranged for trial applications until eligibility is determined.

sources.title: Five days to issue (iPipeline analysis of outstanding requirements)
sources.supports: Across 62 life carriers, average collection time of outstanding requirements: APS orders 19.8 days, paramedical exam 15.2 days, missing application data 10.3 days, APS review 1.4 days, data entry 1.3 days.

sources.title: U.S. Individual Life Accelerated Underwriting Survey 2021 summary results
sources.supports: 43 carriers: full underwriting workflow averages 26 days from application submission to decision (range of averages 5 to 121), accelerated workflow 6 days; AU improves time by about 20 business days.

sources.title: Why does it take so long to get my policies issued?
sources.supports: Canadian placement time fell by four to six days since 2012; some companies report an average of 18 days to obtain an APS; tele-interviews, paramedicals and inspections are rescheduled or need call backs when clients are not prepared; incomplete applications go to a pending queue while the advisor tracks down the client.

sources.title: 5 key enhancements that move the life insurance exam process forward
sources.supports: Agents can book through ScheduleNow when they submit an online exam order, removing follow-up calls to the applicant; texts with links to book, confirmations and reminders with cancel or reschedule options; agents follow open cases in carrier or vendor portals.

sources.title: PIPEDA fair information principle 3: Consent
sources.publisher: Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada
sources.supports: Meaningful consent is required to collect, use and disclose personal information; express consent is generally required for sensitive information; consent can be withdrawn subject to notice.

sources.title: A delay in the attending physician's statement can delay your insurance application
sources.supports: An underwriting service sends the APS request to the physician and follows up about every two weeks; insurers may close the application if the APS stays outstanding; applicants often finish health testing within a few weeks and then wait several more weeks for the APS.

sources.title: Wages: Medical administrative assistant in Ontario (NOC 13112)
sources.supports: Ontario hourly wages low 17.95, median 25.00, high 32.70 dollars (Labour Force Survey 2023-2024); Toronto median 23.00.

sources.title: The model laboratory's insurance testing service scheduler user guide
sources.supports: The self-service tele-interview scheduler launched on 9 January 2023 to remove callouts and telephone tag, improve turnaround and avoid no-shows; advisors can book for the applicant using order identifiers; applicants get email or text links and reminders 24 hours and 1 hour before.

sources.title: Order Management System user tips
sources.supports: Advisors register as requestors or head office administrators; rush orders should give the applicant's primary phone, preferred location, availability and language; partners at the same address can be noted for one visit and orders duplicated; errors found after submission must be phoned in to the office.

sources.title: APS collection
sources.supports: An APS request needs a current and valid authorization from the applicant (some hospitals or physicians require an original signature) and the attending physician's name and address; orders come from the insurer through the secure website; prior fee approval from the insurer and prepayment to the physician where required; forms faxed or couriered; follow-ups on the insurer's contact cycle.

assumptions: One order is one service order. The organisation file's monthly volumes for paramedical (16,000), tele-interview (13,000), APS (8,000) and inspection (1,500) work sum to about the 38,000 orders a month, so routing shares follow those volumes.

Advisors place about 65 percent of orders (paramedicals and most tele-interviews) and insurers about 35 percent (APS and some tele-interviews), based on SOA 2011 and Equitable's rule that the insurer orders the APS and the advisor the other evidence.

Booking the paramedical appointment with the applicant is placed in the paramedical exam process, as the organisation file describes the health professional calling the applicant; the company's web page says a customer care representative contacts the applicant, so in practice some bookings are made centrally.

Tele-interview booking calls are made by case coordinators here; some companies use dedicated schedulers in the tele-interview centre. The self-service scheduler launched in January 2023, so only about 8 percent of 2019-2022 orders arrive with an agreed time.
Partners at the same address are combined into one visit when the advisor notes it, as the ordering tips ask.
Advisor status calls overlap the waits of other steps, so their wait is set near zero and they are marked concurrent with the duplicate check.

Case coordinator FTE (58 of 70) is set close to what hands-on time times volume implies; the organisation file's 70 coordinators also cover examiner follow-up and file release, which leaves them thinly staffed if hands-on times are longer than estimated.
Loaded costs come from the organisation file (hourly wage times 1.35).
Weekend and evening orders wait until the desk opens, which sets the high end of the first queue at about 40 hours.
